name: MineDreamer: Learning to Follow Instructions via Chain-of-Imagination for Simulated-World Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces MineDreamer, a Minecraft agent that imagines stages of an instruction and turns them into keyboard-and-mouse actions in a simulated world.

name: Tell Me What's Next: Textual Foresight for Generic UI Representations
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Textual Foresight learns UI representations by describing the future screen expected after an action on the current interface. The OpenApp dataset supports pretraining and downstream evaluation of representations that connect individual elements with whole-screen changes.

name: Web Agents with World Models: Learning and Leveraging Environment Dynamics in Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses a learned web world model to predict important state changes and compare candidate actions before executing them.

name: Is Your LLM Secretly a World Model of the Internet? Model-Based Planning for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces WebDreamer, which simulates candidate web actions with language-model world models and value estimates before acting.

name: VEM: Environment-Free Exploration for Training GUI Agent with Value Environment Model
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Trains GUI agents with a frozen value model learned from offline interactions, guiding action exploration without predicting complete next observations.

name: Language Models can Self-Improve at State-Value Estimation for Better Search
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The abstract also reports evaluations on multi-hop question answering and math puzzles.
summary: Introduces Self-Taught Lookahead (STL), which trains a value model to predict actions and resulting states for more efficient search, with evaluation on web-agent tasks.

name: ViMo: A Generative Visual GUI World Model for App Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ViMo predicts the next mobile-app screenshot after a candidate action by separately modeling graphics and text. A symbolic placeholder representation preserves layout while a second predictor supplies readable text, enabling visual lookahead for GUI-agent planning.

name: WebEvolver: Enhancing Web Agent Self-Improvement with Coevolving World Model
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WebEvolver trains a co-evolving world model to predict web observations and generate additional agent-training trajectories. The same model supports look-ahead action selection at inference, with evaluation on live web-task benchmarks.

name: Unlocking Smarter Device Control: Foresighted Planning with a World Model-Driven Code Execution Approach
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: FPWC builds and refines a task-oriented world model before planning mobile-device actions. It executes plans as code and evaluates the approach in simulated environments and on real mobile devices.

name: ScreenExplorer: Training a Vision-Language Model for Diverse Exploration in Open GUI World
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Trains ScreenExplorer with reinforcement learning in dynamic GUI environments, using a world-model curiosity reward and experience-stream distillation to support sustained exploration.

name: WebSynthesis: World-Model-Guided MCTS for Efficient WebUI-Trajectory Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its trajectory generation takes place in simulated virtual web environments.
summary: Introduces WebSynthesis, which uses a learned web world model and tree-based planning to synthesize interaction trajectories for training web agents.

name: General Agentic Planning Through Simulative Reasoning with World Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Evaluation covers three task categories within a web-browser environment.
summary: Introduces SiRA, an agent architecture that uses a language-based world model to simulate action outcomes for planning in web-browser tasks.

name: SEAgent: Self-Evolving Computer Use Agent with Autonomous Learning from Experience
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SEAgent explores unfamiliar software using a world-state assessor and an automatically generated task curriculum. It learns from failed and successful interactions through adversarial imitation and GRPO, then combines specialist experience into a generalist agent evaluated on five OSWorld software environments.

name: UISim: An Interactive Image-Based UI Simulator for Dynamic Mobile Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Planning for agent navigation is described as a potential application of the simulator.
summary: Introduces UISim, an image-based mobile UI simulator that predicts the next screen layout after an action and renders the resulting screen for testing and data generation.

name: R-WoM: Retrieval-augmented World Model For Computer-use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: R-WoM evaluates how well world models predict nearby GUI states, align complete procedures, and recognize milestone transitions. It retrieves external tutorials to guide simulated future interactions, with experiments on subsets of OSWorld and WebArena.

name: LLMs as Scalable, General-Purpose Simulators For Evolving Digital Agent Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces UI-Simulator, which generates UI states and transitions for agent-training trajectories, and UI-Simulator-Grow, which prioritizes tasks and trajectory variants.

name: WebATLAS: An LLM Agent with Experience-Driven Memory and Action Simulation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported success rate is measured on WebArena-Lite.
summary: WebATLAS is a web agent that stores interaction outcomes and simulates candidate actions before acting, using past experience to plan navigation on unseen websites.

name: Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). WebArena is one of several environments used to evaluate this general agent training framework.
summary: DreamGym synthesizes agent experiences with a reasoning-based environment model for online RL; its evaluations include the web task setting WebArena.

name: MobileWorldBench: Towards Semantic World Modeling For Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates semantic world models for mobile interfaces and studies natural-language state transitions as a tool for agent planning.

name: MobileDreamer: Generative Sketch World Model for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MobileDreamer predicts post-action GUI states as task-relevant textual sketches with an order-invariant learning objective. Agents use these predictions for lookahead action selection, evaluated on AndroidWorld.

name: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DynaWeb learns a world model that predicts web-page representations after actions and uses it to generate policy-training rollouts. It interleaves these rollouts with expert trajectories and evaluates the trained web agents on WebArena and WebVoyager.

name: Generative Visual Code Mobile World Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: gWorld predicts future mobile GUI states as renderable web code and supplies an automated pipeline for code-based training data. The study evaluates visual state prediction and how stronger world models affect downstream mobile policies.

name: SafePred: A Predictive Guardrail for Computer-Using Agents via World Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.
summary: SafePred uses world-model risk forecasts to guide action filtering and task replanning. Its desktop and web safety evaluations distinguish policy compliance, task success and success under the specified policy.

name: GUI-GenBench: Evaluating Image Generation Models as Interactive GUI Environments
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-GenBench tests image-generation models as action-conditioned GUI environments across five suites, including transitions, trajectories and grounding. Its VLM-based GUI-Score separates goal completion, interaction logic, consistency and visual properties.

name: Code2World: A GUI World Model via Renderable Code Generation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Code2World predicts future GUI screens through renderable code, trained on AndroidCode trajectories with supervised learning and render-aware reinforcement learning. It evaluates visual prediction and downstream AndroidWorld navigation with the learned world model.

name: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebWorld, an open-web simulator trained on interaction trajectories for generating agent training data and testing candidate actions. WebWorld-Bench evaluates simulated transitions, alongside downstream web-agent training experiments.

name: World-Model-Augmented Web Agents with Action Correction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: WAC has a web-agent action model consult a world model, simulate action outcomes and use judge feedback to correct actions before execution.

name: Computer-Using World Model
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents a desktop world model that predicts textual UI changes before synthesizing the next screenshot. It learns from Microsoft Office transitions and is evaluated by letting a frozen agent compare simulated actions before execution.

name: UI-Oceanus: Scaling GUI Agents with Synthetic Environmental Dynamics
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: UI-Oceanus converts autonomous GUI exploration and execution feedback into supervision for predicting future interface states. It compares forward and inverse objectives during continual pretraining and examines downstream offline and online navigation as synthetic data scales.

name: Agentic World Modeling: Foundations, Capabilities, Laws, and Beyond
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Web and GUI agents are one part of a survey that also covers physical, social, and scientific settings.
summary: Survey of agentic world models that classifies predictive capabilities and governing laws, including the digital setting of web and GUI agents.

name: How Mobile World Model Guides GUI Agents?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Compares mobile world models that predict state changes as delta text, full text, images or renderable code. Downstream Android benchmarks examine synthetic training trajectories and test-time guidance, including limits of post-action reflection.

name: MIRAGE: Mobile Agents with Implicit Reasoning and Generative World Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports results on AndroidWorld and AndroidControl.
summary: Introduces MIRAGE, which trains mobile app agents to reason in compact latent states and anticipate future screenshots, reducing generated tokens during action selection.

name: SeerGuard: A Safety Framework for Mobile GUI Agents via World Model Prediction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses instruction screening and a safety-augmented world model to assess likely consequences of mobile GUI actions before execution.

name: EvoGUI: An Evolution-Aware Benchmark for GUI State-Transition Understanding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces EvoGUI, which derives temporal ordering, inverse action/value prediction, and successor-discrimination probes from recorded GUI trajectories. Its web-derived benchmark isolates transition understanding from the other abilities involved in end-to-end task success.

name: Scaling GUI Agents with Visual State Transitions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces State Transition Pretraining, which jointly learns to infer actions from GUI changes and predict future states from current screens and actions. Subsequent instruction-trajectory fine-tuning tests whether these representations transfer to desktop and mobile agent tasks.

name: AppDeltaWorld: Transition-Grounded Delta Code World Model for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AppDeltaWorld predicts executable code updates for the next mobile UI state, using transition-constrained retrieval and rendered visual assets. It evaluates reconstruction fidelity separately from policy training and adaptation using generated environments.

name: GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The main setting is video-game interaction, with GUI control included as an action mode.
summary: Introduces GameWAM, a model for native game play and GUI control that predicts future visuals and keyboard-mouse actions from synchronized gameplay and GUI trajectories.

name: WM-R1: Training GUI Agents to Reason and leverage World Models with Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses learned world models for mobile-agent training rollouts and for reasoning about the consequences of candidate GUI actions.

name: GUI-CC: Benchmarking Contextual Consistency of GUI World Models as Agent Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-CC, a benchmark for assessing GUI world models as multi-step agent environments. Separate reference-action and agent-loop tracks test whether generated screens preserve context, plausible transitions, and task progress throughout interaction.

name: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains discriminative web world models to distinguish the true next state from outcomes of alternative actions. Branching web trajectories support training, followed by tests of predicted-state matching, process-reward action ranking and end-to-end WebArena-Lite selection.

name: The GUI Is Not the State: Diagnosing State Aliasing in GUI World Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces StateAliasBench to isolate GUI world-model ambiguities in which matching visible screens and actions can lead to different futures. It augments frozen world models with structured state recovered from interaction history and evaluates the effect on prediction and agent execution.

name: PrecogUI: Proactive GUI Agents via Pre-cognitive Simulation and Experience Retrieval
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents PrecogUI, which retrieves prior anomaly and success patterns and predicts symbolic UI transitions before choosing actions. It also introduces InterfereBench, generated for evaluating long GUI workflows with disruptive events and recovery requirements.

name: AutoGUIWorld: Image Generators as Visual World Models for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AutoGUIWorld, which combines task planning and image editing to synthesize action-grounded GUI trajectories without running the depicted software. It filters generated transitions and tests whether training on them improves agents operating real desktop and scientific applications.

name: How To Train Your World Model: Fine-tuning vs RAG for LM-based World Modeling
notes: Adjacent cross-domain study with WebShop as its web evaluation. WebShop uses text-rendered search/product pages and an explicit valid-action menu. A frozen policy proposes five actions; a world model predicts their next observations and the policy scores them before one is executed in the simulator. Utility is normalized environment reward, while fidelity uses a model judge; neither is a universal GUI task-success rate. Fine-tuning and retrieval use collected training experience; the hybrid masks same-episode retrieval. The retained Atom and v1 HTML abstract wording differs; original bibliographic metadata and its abstract digest are preserved.
summary: Compares fine-tuned, retrieval-based and hybrid language-model world models for next-observation prediction and action selection in text environments including WebShop.

name: Imagine to Act: High-Fidelity Data Synthesis via Image Editing World Model for Scalable GUI Agent Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Infinite-Dreamer, which learns action-conditioned screenshot editing from structured descriptions of GUI changes and uses it to synthesize robustness examples and multi-step trajectories. The synthetic data trains a mobile GUI agent evaluated on AndroidWorld, MobileWorld, and AndroidControl-Curated.

name: AdvSim2Real : Training Web Agents Against Adaptive Prompt Injection in a Web World Model
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents AdvSim2Real, which jointly adapts web-task curricula, prompt-injection adversaries, and agent policies inside a frozen web world model. It evaluates robustness against an unseen adversary and transfer from simulated interaction to a real browser.

name: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents LGWM, a decoder-free GUI world model that predicts the next screen representation from an action and compares it with the observed state to verify transitions. Its paired diagnostic separates legitimate and hijacked transitions that lead to the same credential screen.

name: Latent World Action Model for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Replaces future-screenshot generation with a shared latent representation for GUI action selection and action-conditioned transition prediction. An action-aware contrastive objective encourages the transition representation to retain discriminative action-induced changes.

name: Beyond Next-Screen Prediction: The Decision Value of GUI World Models
notes: The matched augmentation experiment measures offline ranking; AndroidWorld task-success comparisons use differently trained evaluators, leaving prediction value unisolated. A separate web evaluator is trained on Mind2Web, with mixed web results for direct scoring. The main study concerns one-step selection.
summary: Separates next-screen prediction from action evaluation in GUI lookahead and trains Direct Action Ranking on reference actions, comparing prediction-augmented scoring under matched offline supervision.

name: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The web-agent benchmark is one of two evaluation settings.
summary: PAWM predicts likely multi-step pitfalls and selectively guides black-box agents; its evaluations include a web-agent benchmark.

name: Computer-Use Agents Gain Little Benefit from a World Model When Conditioned on Tutorials
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The finding concerns agents conditioned on tutorials, using OSWorld-Tutorial and ScienceBoard-Tutorial.
summary: RAG-PolicyJudge selects computer-use actions proposed with task-specific tutorials; the study compares its decisions with and without world-model rollouts.

name: MKD2World: A Typed Spatial MarkDown World Model For Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces MKD2World, a desktop web world model that represents interface elements in Typed Spatial Markdown and predicts post-action states, supported by AtomBlock-WebUI annotations.

name: Textual Foresight
summary: Textual Foresight pretrains UI representations by predicting textual descriptions of future screen states resulting from mobile UI actions.

name: AutoCoA
summary: AutoCoA internalizes Chain-of-Action generation into reasoning models via step-level SFT, reinforcement learning, and simulated tool world models.

name: ViMo code
notes: The README describes ViMo as a GUI world model that predicts the next GUI state as image and text. UI_text_prediction.py runs the text-prediction step with Gemini (gemini-2.0-flash), with a GPT-4o variant in the same file. data/ holds the selected Android in the Wild and AndroidControl episode IDs with annotations; images must be downloaded from the original releases, then generate_ocr.py and check_fix.py prepare the symbolic text representation. Graphic prediction is trained by following the InstructPix2Pix project, with edit_cli.py and generate.yaml for inference; no trained weights are in the repository. 'ViMo-Empowered Agent' is a copy of AndroidWorld (with its own Apache-2.0 LICENSE) whose vimo modules post the current screenshot and a candidate action to a world-model server and score the predicted screen when choosing actions. The project page links this repository and arXiv 2504.13936. No license file is at the repository root.
summary: Code for the ViMo GUI world model: Gemini-based next-screen text prediction, AITW and AndroidControl data processing, InstructPix2Pix-style graphic inference, and an AndroidWorld agent that consults it.

name: Code2World
notes: The README provides environment setup and an AndroidWorld run command. It requires pretrained Code2World weights and an OPENAI_API_KEY.
summary: Code2World provides code for predicting the next Android GUI screen from a screenshot and proposed action through renderable code, with an AndroidWorld agent integration.

name: Octopus
summary: Octopus is a vision-language programmer agent trained with environmental feedback to generate executable control code in GTA and Gibson worlds.

details.license_components_note: agent_env/ includes files carrying Apache-2.0 headers from The android_world Authors, for example agent_env/task_evals/single/contacts.py; the root LICENSE is MIT.

name: GUI-Trajectory-Virtual
notes: The README says its arXiv paper is still to come; the GUIGuard project page presents this repository as that paper's trajectory-synthesis workflow, which is the basis for the paper link. In virtual_env_gemini3.py each step sends the previous screenshot and an action description to a chat-completions endpoint and decodes the returned image as the next screen; the code's default model is google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free, while the README examples use google/gemini-3-pro-image-preview. The adapter mocks the accessibility tree and ADB calls. The runner defines 57 social-app task goals whose simplified task class reports success as 1.0 without a check; generated trajectories therefore have unverified outcomes. Nothing was run.
summary: Synthesizes Android agent trajectories without a device: an image model behind a chat-completions API draws each next screen from the previous screenshot and the action chosen by a Mobile-Agent-v3-style agent.

name: LGWM (Latent GUI World Model)
summary: LGWM is an action-conditioned latent GUI world model that predicts next-state representations to verify GUI agent transitions.

name: nanoAWM (Agent World Model Lab)
summary: nanoAWM is an inspectable Agent World Model laboratory for simulating action consequences in long-horizon tool and computer-use agents.

name: WMA Web Agent
notes: The README links world-model and value-model adapters and related datasets. WebArena experiments require its Docker environment; the README names MIT for code and CC BY-NC 4.0 for data.
summary: A web agent uses a learned world model to predict consequential page changes before choosing an action. The repository includes trajectory processing and inference code.

name: WebDreamer
summary: World-model and planning components that simulate web-action outcomes, with linked training data and model checkpoints.

name: Qwen-AgentWorld
notes: The repository holds the AgentWorldBench evaluation script (eval/eval.py) and per-domain world-model and judge system prompts; the Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B weights (MoE, 35B total, 3B active, 256K context) and the AgentWorldBench dataset are hosted on Hugging Face. The README reports training on more than 10M interaction trajectories and gives SGLang, vLLM and Transformers usage.
summary: A language world model that predicts the next environment observation across seven domains, including Android screens, browser pages and desktop accessibility trees, released with AgentWorldBench evaluation code.

name: SEAgent
summary: SEAgent enables computer-use agents to self-evolve in unfamiliar software environments using a World State Model and curriculum task generator.

name: Tencent AI LAB - Self-Improving Agent
notes: The repository lists separate WebEvolver and WebCoT directories and also includes VScan, a visual-token reduction project.
summary: A research code collection for web-agent self-improvement, including WebEvolver's world-model approach and WebCoT's reconstructed reasoning trajectories.

name: RLVR-World
summary: RLVR-World trains world models with verifiable reinforcement learning to predict state transitions for web and game agents.

name: gWorld (GuiWorld)
summary: gWorld is an open-weight 8B/32B mobile GUI world model that predicts next-step screen states via renderable web code generation.

name: Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-value-model-16k-qlora-adapter-v2
notes: PEFT 0.12.0 adapter weights (adapter_model.safetensors) with optimizer, scheduler and trainer-state files for the base model meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The WMA paper trains the value function on Mind2Web with rewards set by progress toward the goal; the card states no license.
summary: QLoRA adapter for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct that acts as the value model of the WMA web agent, rating world-model predictions of each candidate action's outcome so the agent can choose the top-scored one.

name: Dreamer-7B-Shopping
notes: The card names Qwen2-VL-7B as the base model, declares an Apache 2.0 license, and links the WebDreamer repository and paper.
summary: A shopping-domain Dreamer-7B checkpoint for WebDreamer, which uses screenshot-conditioned predictions of candidate web actions to support agent planning.

name: jacklishufan/MobileWorld
notes: One mobileworld.tar of about 184 MB; the README asks users to download and untar it manually. Screenshots come from the separate jacklishufan/aitw and jacklishufan/android_control image datasets, and the README also links the Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-MobileWorld-SFT model. The repository has no card or license.

notes: Two sharded safetensors files and a LICENSE file; the card declares MIT. The RLVR-World lang_wm README merges LoRA weights after SFT, the RLVR-trained counterpart is thuml/webarena-world-model-rlvr, and the paper uses the world model for model predictive control of WebArena agents.
summary: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B fine-tuned as a language world model for WebArena: it predicts which accessibility-tree items change after a web action, trained by SFT on chain-of-thought data before the RLVR stage.

name: jiamingzz/lgwm
notes: The release contains world model weights and a linear harm head. Usage calls the companion code with before and after screenshots and an action JSON file. The card declares an Apache 2.0 license.

summary: Dreamer-7B-Reddit is a Reddit-domain checkpoint for WebDreamer. It predicts the screen state after a proposed action to support web-agent planning.

name: webarena-world-model-rlvr
notes: The repository holds one safetensors checkpoint whose Qwen2 config names DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B as its base path; the card lists thuml/webarena-world-model-sft as base model and thuml/webarena-world-model-cot as dataset. The RLVR-World code base provides GRPO training scripts and a WebArena evaluation that needs self-hosted WebArena sites. License: MIT.
summary: A language world model for web page state prediction on WebArena, post-trained with RLVR from an SFT checkpoint and used for model predictive control of web agents.

name: Mobile-GUI-Worldmodel-SFT
notes: The card lists AITZ, AITW, AMEX, AndroidControl, and GUI-Odyssey archives, plus annotation scripts and evaluation assets.
summary: A mobile GUI dataset for world-model training and evaluation. Its trajectory archives pair screenshots with page-state text and action-formatted training examples.

dataset_profile.notes: Two purpose-specific files are released: webevolver_policy_sft.jsonl and webevolver_world_model_sft.jsonl. The files serve policy-model and world-model purposes; their split relationship, modality and example count remain unspecified.

data.reason: Publisher dataset-card declaration for this release.

data.basis: Publisher dataset-card declaration for this release.

name: WebEvolver SFT data
notes: The card and public manifest identify separate policy-model and world-model JSONL files. The inspected card leaves the row total and complete record schema unstated. MIT is the publisher’s data declaration.
summary: Two JSONL collections for supervised fine-tuning the WebEvolver agent policy and web world model.

name: Dreamer-7B
summary: WebDreamer model checkpoint that predicts the consequences of web actions from screenshots and textual descriptions.

name: gWorld-32B
notes: The repository lists checkpoint shards, processor files, and training state files. The card declares an Apache 2.0 license and links the model's paper and MWMBench.
summary: A released mobile GUI world model that takes a screenshot and an action, then predicts the next interface as renderable HTML. The card identifies Qwen3-VL-32B as its base.

name: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-MobileWorld-SFT
notes: The repository holds four safetensors shards with Qwen3-VL configuration files and no model card. The paper reports fine-tuning for 2 epochs on 8 A6000 GPUs and using the model as the world model of an M3A-based agent on AndroidWorld. The MobileWorldBench repository provides QA and generation evaluation scripts.
summary: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct fine-tuned on the MobileWorld dataset as a semantic world model that describes in natural language how a mobile GUI screen changes after an action, for planning by mobile agents.

dataset_profile.notes: The card reports a cleaned size of 3.12M without defining the counting unit, so no sample total is inferred. The data card declares noncommercial share-alike terms, separately from the model-weight license.

name: Dreamer V1 Data
notes: The card reports a cleaned size of 3.12M without explicitly defining its counting unit. The catalog leaves the exact sample count unknown. Its data license differs from the model-weight license.
summary: Web-world-model training data with prompts, images, action descriptions, and responses, released with the WebDreamer project.

name: LGWM data and RSWT-Bench
notes: The card lists training and validation transition indices, screenshot shards and benchmark train and test splits. It identifies the accompanying paper.
summary: A dataset of GUI screen transitions for training a world model, released with RSWT-Bench to evaluate whether observed screens follow the intended actions.
